findings.evidence: "The ~50–60× envelope around that single geometry is the book's own characterization, not a figure from the report [1P][HYPOTHESIS]"
findings.issue: Provenance label [1P] contradicts the sentence's own explicit statement. The Preface (p.15) defines [1P] as "first-party: the model vendor's own spec." The sentence says "the book's own characterization, not a figure from the report" — i.e. it is NOT from DeepSeek's spec. The provenance should be a book-internal tag (e.g. [ILLUSTRATIVE] or [2°] if interpreting published data), not [1P].
findings.fix_instruction: Replace [1P][HYPOTHESIS] with [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] (or [2°][HYPOTHESIS] if treating it as interpretation of the cited second-hand source). The epistemic status [HYPOTHESIS] is correct; only the provenance axis is wrong.

findings.chapter: Ch 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
findings.evidence: "At 9.2K tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — and the 8-bit raw byte-halving variant is ~12.06 GB — 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB, derived from the exact per-token byte count rather than the rounded 1.31 MB constant (the convention Ch. 7 follows); the 8-bit variant is not ~13.4 GB, because that is the overhead-inclusive estimate — 12.06 GB × 1.11 ≈ 13.39 GB, from adding an assumed ~11% block/metadata overhead to the raw tensor bytes (the ~11% is [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the 13.39 GB is [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED])"
findings.issue: The 8-bit/FP8 KV figure is quoted at two different precisions in the same paragraph and across the book: 12.06 GB here (9,200 tokens, input-only) and 12.45 GB in Ch. 7 Table 7-1 ('FP8 total inference KV (9.5K max, resident basis) ≈ 12.45 GB'). Ch. 1's paragraph gives no indication that the 12.06 GB is the input-only basis, so a reader taking 'the 8-bit variant' as the per-request resident footprint understates the slot-counting figure that Ch. 7 and Ch. 17 use. Ch. 7 §7.3 explicitly names the two bases ('Per-request KV is quoted on two named bases: ~24.1 GB at the 9.2K input-only prefill ... and ~24.9 GB (byte-accurate 24.90368 GB) at the 9.5K input-plus-output resident slot'), but Ch. 1 does not name the basis of its 12.06 GB figure at all, creating an apparent 0.39 GB contradiction for the same '8-bit variant' of the same request.
findings.fix_instruction: In Ch. 1's KV-cache paragraph, name the basis explicitly for the 8-bit figure: '~12.06 GB at the 9.2K input-only basis; ~12.45 GB on the 9.5K input-plus-output resident basis that Ch. 7 uses for slot counting', and cross-reference Ch. 7 §7.3 for the rounding convention. Apply the same basis-naming to the FP16 figure in the same sentence so the pair reads symmetrically.

findings.chapter: Ch 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
findings.evidence: "That 8-bit figure is the raw tensor byte-halving of the FP16 value: 1.31 MB/token vs 2.62 MB/token, exactly 50%, with any block-allocation/metadata overhead NOT vendor-measured here and to be filled by a deployment benchmark."
findings.issue: The '1.31 MB/token' rounding is used in a ratio claim ('exactly 50%') while the exact byte count is 1,310,720 B vs 2,621,440 B. 1.31/2.62 = 0.5000 exactly at the printed precision, so the ratio holds; however the same chapter prints '~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB) per token at 8-bit (~2.5 MiB, 2.62 MB at FP16)' earlier on page 31, and Ch. 7 states the canonical constant as '~2.62 MB (exactly 2.5 MiB/token)'. The dual-unit presentation (MiB and MB) for the same quantity — 2.5 MiB = 2.62 MB — is used repeatedly across Chs. 1, 3, 7, 17 and is the kind of quantity a reader will lift into a sizing slide; the book states the convention once (Ch. 1: 'MiB = 2^20 bytes and MB = 10^6 bytes') but Ch. 7's Table 7-1 mixes them inside a single row ('2 ×80 ×8192 ×2 B ≈ 2.62 MB = 2,560 KiB = 2.5 MiB'), where '2,560 KiB' is a third spelling of the same number and is not defined anywhere. This makes the load-bearing KV constant (which sets the entire fleet-sizing chain) hard to lift without ambiguity.
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one unit for the KV constant across Chs. 1/3/7/17 (recommend MB, since the book's token-count convention is SI), state the conversion once, and remove the undefined '2,560 KiB' spelling from Table 7-1.

findings.chapter: Ch 1 (It All Starts With the First Token)
findings.evidence: Ch 1, PDF p.27: 'the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model — this book's reading of the vendor line-ups above, not a vendor statement [2°][HYPOTHESIS].' Compare the same class of book-own reading of first-party sources tagged [1P] elsewhere: Ch 1, PDF p.32 ('...is, on this book's reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope... [1P][HYPOTHESIS]. That reading is the book's own, not a vendor-stated interpretation') and Ch 6, PDF p.150 ('not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient — on this book's own reading of that post's Table 3, not a vendor-stated interpretation [1P][HYPOTHESIS]').
findings.issue: Provenance-axis mismatch: the claim is the book's own inference drawn from [1P] model cards (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4 — cited as [1P][FACT] in the same sentence), but it is tagged [2°], which the book defines as 'reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark'. The document's own established pattern for identical book-own readings of first-party sources is [1P][HYPOTHESIS] (Ch 1 p.32, Ch 6 p.150), so the [2°] tag is both wrong per the axis definition and internally inconsistent.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-tag the sentence as [1P][HYPOTHESIS] (provenance = the vendor cards the reading is drawn from), or drop the provenance tag and keep [HYPOTHESIS] alone; do not use [2°] for the book's own interpretation.

findings.evidence: Page 31, Table 'Family... Bytes/token' row 'Reduced-width per-token'. Derivation: 'for full MHA: 2·n_h·d_h = 2×128×128 = 32,768'. Comparison: 'for MLA: d_c + d_h^R = 512+64 = 576'. Ratio claim: 'so 32,768/576 ≈ 56.9 ≈ 57×'.
findings.issue: Arithmetic Error / Unit Mismatch. The 'Full MHA' value (32,768) includes a factor of 2 for K and V tensors ($2 \times n_h \times d_h$), whereas the 'MLA' value (576) appears to be a single concatenated latent vector ($d_c + d_h^R$) missing the factor of 2. If MLA stores both K and V latents, the correct denominator is 1,152, resulting in a ratio of ~28.5×, not 57×. The text compares a total storage metric against a per-tensor storage metric, inflating the efficiency claim by 2x.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-evaluate the MLA geometry formula from DeepSeek-V2 paper. If $d_c + d_h^R$ represents the latent size for a single projection (e.g. key), multiply by 2 to get total KV state. Adjust the derived ratio (~28x vs ~57x) and correct the text's claim about KV cache shrinkage.
